label: JZ Mock D · Paper 1 · Question 12
source: JZ Mock D · Paper 1 · Question 12 · Publisher worked solution
knowledgePattern: Track a parabola vertex through rotations about specified centres

hints.title: Track the turning point
hints.body: Complete the square in both curve equations to find their vertices. A rotation sends the first vertex to the final vertex.
hints.recap: Completing the square shows the turning point of a quadratic.
hints.pitfall: These equations give <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> in terms of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow></math>; still write coordinates in the order <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.
hints.pause: Mark the first vertex, the final vertex and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> on a sketch.

recall.reminder: Completing the square shows the turning point of a quadratic.

hints.title: Measure from the centre of rotation
hints.body: Measure the horizontal and vertical distances from P1 to the first vertex. Under a clockwise quarter-turn, right becomes down and up becomes right.
hints.recap: For a rotation about a point, rotate the displacement from that point.
hints.pitfall: Do not rotate about the origin unless the stated centre is the origin.
hints.pause: Find the vertex after the first rotation.

recall.reminder: For a rotation about a point, rotate the displacement from that point.

hints.title: Repeat with the unknown centre
hints.body: Write P2=(a,5). Measure from this centre to the vertex you just found, and turn that displacement clockwise again.
hints.recap: A clockwise quarter-turn sends a displacement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.
hints.pitfall: Add the centre coordinates back after rotating the displacement.
hints.pause: Make the resulting coordinates equal to the final vertex and solve for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math>. Check both coordinates.

recall.reminder: A clockwise quarter-turn sends a displacement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.

solution:
1. Complete squares: the first curve is x=(y−4)2+3, with vertex (3,4); the final curve is x=−(y−1)2−6, with vertex (−6,1). Rotations carry the vertex to the vertex.

2. A clockwise quarter-turn sends a displacement (u,v) to (v,−u). Relative to (1,2), the initial vertex has displacement (2,2); it therefore moves to (1,2)+(2,−2)=(3,0).

3. Write P2=(a,5). The next displacement is (3−a,−5), which rotates to (−5,a−3). Adding the centre gives (a−5,a+2)=(−6,1), so a=−1. Answer A.

4. As a full-curve check, these centres produce X=−3−x, Y=5−y. Substituting into the original equation gives X=−Y2+2Y−7, as required.
